title: Simple harmony, melody and rhythm in New Orleans music
summary: Harmony was simplified; melody and rhythm distinguish New Orleans music, unlike bop.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young

blocks.x: Well, what about the harmonic structure? I mean, how is this...

Well, the harmony, in general, down here was always simplified. That's why some people think the musicians were uneducated, but not necessarily. But they, as a rule, they would simplify rather than develop. The harmony didn't seem to be as important as the melody and the rhythm, those two elements. Usually, European music is considered as having melody, rhythm, and harmony. But the melody and the rhythm, I'd say, are the two main factors that you can distinguish New Orleans music. They always stick to the melody. They always have a melody going. Yeah. It isn't like bop or some other music that just has just plain rhythm like a lot of... Sometimes they do riffing and all here, too, but some forms of jazz, it has very little melody. You just get on a little phrase or on a certain little motive and repeat it over and over again. Well, that could be a melody, too. But, I mean, here, they usually like to have a regular tune, something that the people can actually hear and whistle and hum, you know.
